Timeline::set_hour¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::set_hour(int hour) const

Replace The Local Hour¶

set_hour() replaces the hour in every defined element’s local wall clock. The accepted range is [0, 23]; 24 is not an alternate spelling for the following midnight. Date, minute, second, nanoseconds, timezone, rank, and shape remain unchanged.

Use this method when the hour itself is the rule, for example to place events at local 06:xx while retaining their existing minutes and seconds. Use elapsed duration arithmetic when the rule is instead “six hours later.”

Example: Retain The Smaller Clock Fields¶

const auto t = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-01-15T23:58:59.123456789Z", "2024-06-20T04:05:06.000000004Z"},
    {"2024-09-28T12:30:45.900000000Z", "2024-12-01T00:00:00.000000001Z"},
});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(t.set_hour(6), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2024-01-15T06:58:59.123456789+00:00", "2024-06-20T06:05:06.000000004+00:00"], 
  ["2024-09-28T06:30:45.900000000+00:00", "2024-12-01T06:00:00.000000001+00:00"]
]

The method changes 23, 04, 12, and 00 to 06; it does not zero the smaller fields. Chain set_minute() and set_second() when the complete clock must be replaced.

Example: Local Time Is Not A Fixed UTC Shift¶

const auto ny = pluss::timeline::make("2024-07-01T16:45:00Z")
                    .tz_convert("America/New_York");
std::cout << pluss::timeline::format(ny.set_hour(9), "%F %T %z").at(0) << '\n';

Output¶

2024-07-01 09:45:00 -04:00

The source displays as local 12:45; replacement makes it local 09:45. The operation edits the wall clock under the retained timezone rather than subtracting three hours from every UTC tick by definition.

Daylight-Saving Gaps¶

Some local hours do not exist. Replacement is strict in that case:

try {
  const auto ny = pluss::timeline::make("2024-03-10T06:30:00Z")
                      .tz_convert("America/New_York");
  (void)ny.set_hour(2);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "nonexistent local time rejected\n";
}

Output¶

nonexistent local time rejected

On that date the local clock jumps from 01:59:59 to 03:00:00, so 02:30 cannot be represented. The method does not shift it forward silently. During a fall-back overlap, the first occurrence is selected. NaT remains NaT.

See Also¶

  • hour: inspect the local hour.

  • set_minute: replace the minute field.

  • tz_convert: choose the local calendar before editing it.
